canonical_definition: Temporal Reasoning is the ability to understand, infer, and logically deduce relationships between events across time, encompassing temporal dependencies (e.g., order, causality, simultaneity), dynamic patterns in sequential data (e.g., video streams, evolving knowledge graphs), and time-sensitive generalizations (e.g., arithmetic, scheduling, long-term relations). It involves analyzing event sequences, contextual changes, and temporal hierarchies to answer questions about timing, causation, or state transitions, with applications spanning video understanding, real-time knowledge adaptation, and multi-hop temporal inference. Some definitions emphasize causal reasoning (e.g., explaining action sequences) or domain-specific challenges (e.g., long-context dependencies, visual time arithmetic), but all center on temporal structure as a core axis of reasoning.
